subphase: safe-c33/b84 review: re-establish the seven rows the b84 closures leave BLOCKED at f1c54715b (five `copyctx` rows in src/provider/digest.rs and two in src/provider/legacyprov.rs; none of them in a file this batch edited)
reviewer: closing measurement subagent (not the author of the b84 source change)

venue.attestation: the first element-7 attempt ran without OPENSSL_RS_COURT_DATA and died with MemoryError at the 4 GiB default; it is recorded, not retried, and every later heavy command exports the cap

method: each row is re-derived, not restated: the boundary's operation is resolved with the instrument's own resolver at the candidate commit, the carried coordinate is re-resolved at the ancestor head the chain names, the census's per-site attribution is read from the fresh b84 inventory, and the accepting binding is read from the b84b closures. The four questions are answered per operation from the boundary's own contract and from the span-hash equality.

instrument_findings.what: the element-7 probe failed at b84 with one target-bounded site: `msblob2key_decode.llvm.4118211668640549643 call *0x18(%rax)`, reason base-slot-partial
instrument_findings.cause: the E7-BS witness selects its site by a literal VA or by (symbol leaf, offset).  The b84 rebuild moved the descriptor call from +0x350 to +0x322 (0x52a9c2 - 0x52a6a0) and moved the VA, so neither selector matched.  The rcu pair still matched (+0x5A8, 0x26a418 = 0x269e70 + 0x5A8).
instrument_findings.fix: E7BS_MSBLOB_SITE = 0x52A9C2 and E7BS_MSBLOB_SITE_PIN = ('msblob2key_decode', 0x322); the self-test fixture's call site moved to the same offset so a stale pin still fails the self-test.  The witness body is unchanged, so no contract class is widened.
evidence: court/freeze-b84/e7-ssh-b84.log (FAIL before the re-pin; the first attempt's MemoryError is in the same log)
court/freeze-b84/selftest-b84b.log (E7BS matrix: all eleven mutations fail as required)

instrument_findings.what: the seven rows' content-migration witness found no hop: every carried coordinate was a definition at a head older than the 12-hop window
instrument_findings.cause: MIGRATION_CHAIN_LIMIT was 12 and the chain is now 13 links deep because each carried-forward batch adds its own receipt.  The defining head for these rows (b76c, 0238c6e4adbc) moved from hop 12 to hop 13 at this batch.
instrument_findings.fix: MIGRATION_CHAIN_LIMIT = 32.  This is a work bound, not a safety condition: every hop is still proved individually (coordinate is a definition at that hop's own head, the head is an ancestor, the qualified context matches, and the normalised text hashes to the boundary's declared span).

answers.a_safe_rust_can_cause_ub: No. The operation is an `unsafe extern "C" fn` whose preconditions are supplied by the core through OSSL_FUNC_DIGEST_COPYCTX: both regions are live for `inctx`, `inctx` readable and `outctx` writable, and the call copies exactly that many bytes with `ptr::copy`, so the core's self-copy arm (`copyctx(algctx, algctx)`) is a defined overlapping copy rather than an aliasing violation. No safe-Rust caller reaches the operation except through that method table, and the declared precondition set is exactly what the ABI guarantees. The boundary's own established_by records the C ABI reference, the caller that never manufactures an algctx, the passing self-copy test and the negative control (replacing `ptr::copy` with `ptr::copy_nonoverlapping` turns the same-region call into a violation).
answers.b_all_unsafe_covered: Yes. The operation's only unsafe operations are the `unsafe extern "C"` qualifier, the `ptr::copy` call and the pointer casts that the contract licenses; each is covered by the boundary contract above. The boundary's criteria (contract, caller_or_abi_establishment, safe_rust_interface) are all PASS in the v1i receipt, and the operation text is byte-identical to the span that review read: the span hash re-derived at this candidate, c639719ffc5bdf36a8f78077d4efe08897182c0802b16f900d16a49bf6cc1254, equals the boundary's recorded `span_sha256` exactly, so this batch changes no unsafe operation inside the span.
answers.c_hidden_obligation: None. This batch changes neither the operation's text, its signature, its method-table slot, nor the ABI type of its members; the span hash equality is the evidence, not an inspection claim. No new caller, alias, layout, lifetime or secret-handling obligation is introduced by the row's re-binding: the row moved from BLOCKED to DISCHARGED because a *provenance* walk reached the ancestor head, not because a contract changed.
answers.d_load_bearing_control: Three controls ran. (1) Firing control on this exact row: the b84 closures recorded 7 BLOCKED with `span-unparsable ... neither a definition ... nor inside the boundary's resolved span`, so the detector is not blind to an unreachable provenance coordinate; the same predicate then accepted the row. (2) The element-7 probe fired on the re-pinned E7BS witness before the re-pin (`TARGET-BOUNDED ... msblob2key_decode ... base-slot-partial`) and passed after it, so the pin is load-bearing rather than decorative.
